stages.ix_title: Complete the word with the correct final consonant blend
stages.choice_rule: Four unique lowercase final blends from nd, nt, mp, st, sk, ft, nk, lt, ld, lk, lp, lf, rd, rk, rn, xt, and pt. The stem is a kid sentence with the target word cut before its final blend, so pond shows as po. The cut-off piece must be on the roots word list or in allowed_extra_words, and every other stem word must be on the roots word list. Exactly one blend completes a real word that fits. Set explain_key to final_ plus that blend. If a picture helps, add media as the target lemma and do not describe it.

gold_items.stem: The duck is in the po.
A bird is in the ne.
The la is on at night.
The book is on the de.
We put the coins in the ba at home.
The kids like to play in the hot sa.

roots: The stem keeps a word with its final consonant blend cut off, and that blend is the one right choice.
Wrong choices are other final blends of two or three letters, not single letters and not whole words.
Never use the digraphs sh, ch, th, wh, ck, or ng as choices. A blend keeps each letter.
Do not use nch or tch. The ch in them is a digraph, not a final blend.
Tier 1 wrong blends must not spell any real word with the cut-off piece.
Tier 2 may include one blend that spells a real word the sentence does not mean.
Tier 3 uses two near-miss blends that each spell a different real word.
Exactly one choice may make the sentence true for a child at school, home, or play.
Choices are lowercase letter blends. Do not write the finished word in a choice.
Use kid-world stems only: school, home, food, pets, play, family, or weather. No brands.
Never write a real child name. If a stem needs a name, use <NAME> and names.txt.

tier_rules.1: Short stems of four to six words. Cut the target word before its final blend. Only the right blend spells a real word.
tier_rules.2: Stems of five to eight words. One wrong blend may spell a real word that does not fit the sentence.
tier_rules.3: Stems of seven to ten words. Two wrong blends are near misses that spell a different real word.
